diphoton production at the LHC is a promising channel to test the ADD model, but only if the analysis cuts are chosen carefully and a parton shower is matched to the fixed order calculation.
the diphoton channel is a promising search channel for ADD, with the most sensitive range being d = 3–5.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the diphoton channel is a competitive probe of the ADD model at the LHC.
the diphoton production rate is very small in the ADD model and the current data are not constraining the model.

The main takeaway from our work is that

the ADD model can be excluded at 95% CL up to d = 4 for a cut-based search strategy, and up to d =6 for a search strategy based on the transverse momentum of the photons, if the ADD scale is M s = 3 TeV.
